title: How safe are MCP for AI game development?
author: dhbs90
selftext:
I've been looking into using MCP with Claude or Gemini for Blender, Godot, and Unity to speed up game development.

My main concern is security. From what I understand, some MCP servers can execute Python code or system commands, potentially accessing files outside the game project.

I'd love to let AI build, test, and debug games more independently, but I'm not comfortable giving it unrestricted access to my PC.

How are you guys handling this? Are you using VMs, separate Windows accounts, sandboxing, or just trusting the MCP servers?

Are there any MCP setups you'd actually consider safe enough for game development?

comments.author: 36Celsius
comments.body: No .exe you run on your computer is safe. I don't think MCP are worsts

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: I have no idea about other people's workflows or what they've had happen to them. But so far Claude has only accessed folders I've given it permission to access. If it needs to access a folder outside of that, it asks me permission first. I run blender mcp, mixar mcp, and a couple others and I haven't had an issue

replies.author: Gibgezr
replies.body: Like everything with LLMs, it works until it doesn't.

comments.author: selfish_meme
comments.body: I am using Claude Code with Unreal Engine and Blender via MCP and not. Personally I would do without MCP unless there is totally something you need to do that only the MCP allows

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: I don’t run AI agents on my main computer. I have an old computer that I use for it. The AI can destroy this computer for all I care, I can just wipe the operating system and reinstall.

comments.author: Latent_Space_Cadet
comments.body: Who is going to tell him?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: mcp is just an api, its no different then letting an llm run a python or other script directly. Don't use public mcp servers you don';t know about, once that start locally that you start and know what they are safe. llms in general aren't fool proof you should isolate them or understand the risk that they can delete anything from a file you don't want, to the entire project, or really anything ... thats unlikely more unrelated to the project but it can happen

comments.author: meanjeans99
comments.body:
I just switched my work flow to run claude in a VM that I access using herdr.  The project folders are synced with syncthing. I had it build a service on a spare machine with a GPU that runs as a nobody user on that system.  That service runs blender with MCP so it can still access GPU resources.  If claude makes a mistake and deletes project files or blows up the VM it doesn't effect anything else on my LAN and I have extra copies of the project data via syncthing.

I've never had a problem but the reality is it COULD delete anything you have rights to delete and there a lot of ways for it to get around shell hooks (writing python scripts that delete things, etc).

comments.author: meanjeans99
comments.body:
This is not true.  I've asked claude many times to stay in the project folder and it will still occasionaly run a command outside of it.  The more I looked in to hooks the conclusion I came to is there are ways around that too if it WANTS to.

A separate machine or VM is much safer and if you want to go next level, put that VM in a DMZ.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
You dont really need some explicit MCP setup on your machine these days. There are still advantages to it i.e. having access to MCP config

but claude/gemini/GPT these days can just use MCP on their end or use your computer directly

i.e. AI once tried to do something with Unity and realized that Unity doesn't want to reload unless the window regains the focus (classic Unity behavior) and the AI was like "fine, I will take over the mouse and click the window..." it was hilarious...

comments.author: GT86
comments.body:
I had my agent create an additional bridge from the Godot MCP so it could actually play test the game properly. I kept finding bugs because it was only just doing individual screenshots and not using the UI buttons. 

It found 16 bugs itself within 5 minutes of getting the bridge setup. Pretty happy with that. Much easier to move forward now.
